_added_5_oct.proofShowsCorrection: The proofShows fields in the frozen candidates file overclaim and are left as frozen. Corrected for kinder-rejection: the live check for a text proof is told only to pass an honest, on-topic attempt (src/lib/verify-proof.ts, the TEXT proofs block and the closing line of the system prompt, and line 386 which sends any proof with no photo down the lenient path). It is not told to enforce 'one or two sentences' or 'kind'. It sees one answer at a time, so a copied answer is invisible to it. Nothing tells it to look for text written by a language model, or to reject an answer that carries personal detail. So the proof can show that an answer is on topic and looks like an honest attempt, and no more.

_written: 2026-10-04 night run, branch night/favour-cleanup-20261004. Revised four times on 2026-10-05 after four cold reads.
_count_note: The brief asked for 10 to 15 favours. 14 were drafted. After four independent reads, 2 remain. That is below the 10 to 15 asked for. The others placed a person in a town, at a spot or at a time, or showed a third party's details, or could not be checked by anything. Fewer good rows beat more risky ones. Later on 5 Oct, 15 more were drafted and frozen; 1 of them (kinder-rejection) was kept by the author and by one independent reader. Total: 2 reviewed rows plus 1 added and independently read, 3 against 10 to 15.
_known_limits: For a text favour the live check passes any honest, on-topic attempt, so points are paid for engagement, not for quality. Source: src/lib/verify-proof.ts, the system prompt's TEXT proofs block and its last line, and line 386. The check sees one answer at a time, so a copy is invisible. Nothing in it covers text written by a language model. This applies to translate-line and to kinder-rejection.
Nothing shows that a photo is the sender's own. A picture found online passes as easily as one just taken. The app has no provenance check and this pack does not add one.

The check is a model, not a person. For a flagged TEXT proof on a house favour the code holds no human review at all: the jury appeal takes only a proof with a photo (src/lib/jury-appeal.ts isAppealable), and the confirm route needs the poster's own session, and a house agent is not a person. For a flagged PHOTO proof on a points favour an appeal route exists (/api/jury/appeal, three qualified judges), but no screen in the branch calls it (grep of src/components and src/app). Whether anyone has ever ruled an appeal on the live app is unverified. Each row says what that model can see in the proof and what it cannot. Whether the live model judges these rows well is unverified: none has been posted.

Answers come from one wallet. Several answers from the same wallet add up. That is why no row asks for a town, a spot, a day or a time any more: a town beside photos of real spots, from one wallet, gives a home town and a set of places.
A photo is never placeless. A shelf label can still show a chain name, a branch code, a language. The safety clause in each row is an instruction to the sender. Nothing enforces it.

The personal data check that the review test runs is a reviewer's aid. It caught 5 of 20 unsafe asks written after it was frozen and wrongly flagged 3 of 20 safe ones. A green test does not mean a row is safe.

Both rows were read by a fourth cold reader in their current wording. He found nothing new in staple-prices beyond what is stated, and for translate-line that anyone with a translator can collect its points. Before that reading the wording had been read by no one but the drafter. A person must read every row before it is posted.
No funder, sponsor or requester exists. Each row would post under a house agent name, which can read as someone wanting the data. Nobody does.
_shape: description, category, points, deadlineHours, maxCompletions, agentId and location are a FavourSpec (src/lib/board-replenish.ts validateFavourSpec). ONLY description reaches the person. safety is a clause that is part of description, repeated here so the review test can find it. The other fields are review notes and are not posted.
_reward_note: points are FAVOUR house points, not money. No sponsor or funder exists for any row, so every row is marked unfunded draft. No row promises a payout.
_demand_note: whoWouldWantIt is a plausible requester, written by the drafter. It is not observed demand. No user asked for these.
_review_note: The review test (src/__tests__/favour-pack.test.ts) is an aid. Its personal data check is a pattern matcher that caught 5 of 20 unsafe asks written after it was frozen, and wrongly flagged 3 of 20 safe ones. A green test does not mean a row is safe. A person must read every row before it is posted.

_decisions_for_oscar: translate-line: a machine translation passes. 100 replies at 12 points is 1200 house points that anyone with a translator can collect. Post it as it is, lower the reply count, or drop it.
The pack holds 2 rows against 10 to 15 asked for. Accept 2, or ask for more rows with a person reading each one before it is posted.
Nothing shows a photo is the sender's own. Decide whether any photo favour should be posted before the app can tell.

Finding: the proof screen tells a flagged sender on a points favour 'No points yet. People check it by hand, and the points land if they clear it.' (src/components/Feed.tsx line 3730) and 'Waiting for a human check' (line 3631). For a text proof no code path lets a person check it. For a photo proof the appeal route exists and no screen calls it. Decide whether to change that sentence or build the check. App copy was not changed.

For a text favour the live check pays for an on-topic attempt, not for a good answer. Decide whether translate-line and kinder-rejection should carry points on that basis, and at how many replies. The reader suggests 10 to 20 replies, not 50 or 100.

favours.description: Photo the shelf price labels for a litre of milk and a loaf of bread in a shop. Name the country. Labels only: no people, no receipts, no shop sign.
favours.safety: Labels only: no people, no receipts, no shop sign.
favours.checkedBy: the live model check, not a person
favours.proofShows: Two shelf labels with prices and a currency that can be read.
favours.proofCannotShow: Who took the photo. Nothing shows it is the sender's own and not one found online. Not when it was taken, and not that it is from the country named. A label can carry a chain name; the clause asks to leave the shop sign out and nothing enforces it.
favours.proofRequired: One or two photos with both shelf labels readable. Note: the country only. The first versions asked for the town; a town beside a photo of a real shop, from one wallet, placed the person.
favours.whoWouldWantIt: Anyone comparing the cost of living between countries. A person about to move. A price tracker that has no shelf data.

favours.description: Translate this line into another language you speak, and name the language. The line: "Show your proof, earn your points." Nothing about you is needed.
favours.proofKind: text the model can check against the posted line
favours.checkedBy: the live model check, not a person
favours.proofShows: That the answer is on topic and looks like an honest attempt at a translation. The live check is told to pass any honest on-topic text answer. A model could judge accuracy from the two texts, but this check is not told to, so a poor translation can pass.
favours.proofCannotShow: That the sender speaks the language or wrote it: a machine translation passes. Naming a language is a small fact about the sender, and the ask says another language you speak, not the one spoken at home. Whether the live model check judges this well is unverified.
favours.proofRequired: A text answer: the translated line and the name of the language.
favours.rewardConsequence: A machine translation passes, so this row pays for work a translator can do. 100 replies at 12 points is 1200 house points that anyone with a translator can collect, one reply per wallet. Whether that is acceptable is a decision for Oscar.
favours.whoWouldWantIt: The FAVOUR team, for a first translated screen. Live answers on 4 Oct came in Spanish, Indonesian, Tagalog and Japanese (source: raw/api_tasks.json proof notes).
